reason: The quoted line is verbatim correct: YamlFiles.java:226 reads `if (thin && (arenaKeys.isEmpty() || sawRichArena)) {`, with `thin` computed at :225 as `arenaKeys.stream().allMatch(ARENA_TRUNCATION_ALLOWED_KEYS::contains)` where the allow-list is `Set.of("world")` (:391). A world-only arena is genuinely legal on the load side: readDefinition (:553-618) requires only `world` (requiredString :555) and falls back to Builder initial values for absent `game` (ArenaDefinition.Builder defaults min 2 / max 6 / waves 20 / interval 30, :239-242), while validationFailure (:520-551) explicitly permits `core == null` and empty spawn lists, so such an arena loads and registers. I re-implemented the validator body verbatim and ran it against the real Paper 1.21.4 + snakeyaml 2.2 on synthetic arenas.yml texts: `arena1` rich then `arena2: {world: ...}` returns "arena 'arena2' has only [world] - looks like a truncated write", the exact same two sections in reversed order return null, and a lone world-only arena returns null - so the outcome depends purely on file order, not on sorted order, because ConfigurationSection.getKeys(false) is backed by LinkedHashMap (verified by javap on MemorySection) which preserves document order. The failure really does quarantine rather than warn: YamlFiles.load (:95-98) calls quarantine, which does `Files.move(file.toPath(), corrupt.toPath(), REPLACE_EXISTING)` (:143) and returns Loaded(null, SUSPECT, ...), YamlFileGate.load (:52-61) latches readOnly, and ArenaManager.load (:135-140) logs 'arenas.yml is unusable' and executes registry.clear(), so all arenas disappear. The mid-session path is also real: AdminDeployManager.saveSpawnPoints checks `gate.writable()` at :458 BEFORE `gate.load()` at :471, so the check passes, load() then quarantines the live file and sets the latch, and the subsequent isReadOnly test at :474 aborts the save - i.e. a plain /hilltop deploy addspawn renames the running configuration out from under the server. Two supporting details in the finding are overstated but do not change reachability: the shipped header's step 2 says to fill `world / core / waiting-location` (arenas.yml:8), not world alone, and `/hilltop reloadconfig` does not re-read arenas.yml at all (HilltopCommandHandler.java:396-453 never calls arenaManager.reload(); arenas.yml:92 and README.md:392 both say a restart is required) - it only calls gate.reset() at :404, so the real mid-session triggers are the gate.load() calls inside write paths, not reloadconfig by itself. The complete config does survive as arenas.yml.corrupt (quarantine moves, never truncates), which keeps this at high rather than critical, but on the next start ensureFile() (:841-854) sees no arenas.yml and saveResource() writes the factory template, so the operator is left running factory arenas unless they manually restore the .corrupt file.
